title: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict
abstract: arXiv:2611.21784v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Studies of how long code from AI coding agents survives after it is merged reach conflicting verdicts: agent code is reported to be retained longer than human code, about as long, or modified sooner. Each study makes defensible measurement choices, but how much these choices decide the verdict is unknown. We revisit the survival of agent-attributed code in our earlier study: 854,139 lines that 2,802 merged pull requests (PRs) added to 215 repositories of the AIDev dataset. We vary nine measurement choices in five research questions and build a specification curve of 88 survival analyses, tested under three variance estimators, several observation windows, and permuted labels. For code from human-supervised agents, mostly GitHub Copilot, the choices change the size of the effect but not its direction. For code from the fully-autonomous agent Devin, they decide the verdict. Across repositories, 15 of 22 specifications report it modified

translated_title: 重新审视智能体代码的存续：测量方法的选择如何决定结论
tldr: 本研究通过在854,139行智能体代码上构建包含88项生存分析的规范曲线，发现测量方法的选择仅影响有人类监督的智能体（如GitHub Copilot）代码存续性结论的效应大小，却会完全决定全自主智能体（如Devin）代码的最终结论。
en_tdlr: By constructing a specification curve of 88 survival analyses over 854,139 lines of agent-attributed code, this study shows that measurement choices alter only the effect size for human-supervised agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot) but entirely determine the verdict for fully-autonomous agents (e.g., Devin).
